clues: Oscar was not second in line.
The first spot in line did not belong to Jonah.
Whoever stood fourth in line was either Jonah or Nadia.
Elsa was somewhere ahead of Oscar in line.
Elsa and Milo did not stand next to each other.
Nadia stood somewhere behind Oscar in line.
hints: Look at Oscar's row. Three clues name him, and clue 3 decides who can be fourth. Which spots are left for him?
Clue 4 puts someone ahead of Oscar and clue 6 puts someone behind him, so which ends are ruled out? Then add what clues 1 and 3 cross out.
Clues 4 and 6 keep Oscar off both ends, and clues 1 and 3 rule out second and fourth. So Oscar held the third spot.

solution.key_idea: Clues 4 and 6 keep Oscar off both ends, and clues 1 and 3 rule out second and fourth, so Oscar was third.
steps: Clue 4 puts Elsa ahead of Oscar and clue 6 puts Nadia behind him, so Oscar was neither first nor fifth.
Clue 1 rules out second for Oscar, and clue 3 rules out fourth, so Oscar held the third spot.
By clue 4, Elsa held first or second. Milo cannot hold either one: one is Elsa's, the other is next to her (clue 5).
Clue 3 keeps Milo off fourth, so Milo was fifth, and Nadia, behind Oscar by clue 6, was fourth.
Jonah was not first (clue 2), so he was second, and Elsa was first in line.
solution.epilogue: Elsa had been on the steps since seven, so first pick of the rare books was hers: a 1902 tide almanac. The other four agreed, after some firm whispering from Wren.

tip: Small X's add up: four clues that each cross out one spot can leave a single dot.
answer_line: Elsa gets first pick of the rare books.
